definitions.explanation: The feeling of truly experiencing or understanding something firsthand.
Coming to truly understand or feel the reality of something.

examples.japanese: {合格|ごうかく}した{実感|じっかん}がまだない。
examples.english: I don't yet feel like I've really passed.
examples.notes: 実感がない = doesn't feel real yet

examples.japanese: {親|おや}になって{初|はじ}めて{親|おや}のありがたさを{実感|じっかん}した。
examples.english: I truly realized how precious parents are only after becoming a parent myself.

examples.japanese: {景気|けいき}{回復|かいふく}の{実感|じっかん}がない。
examples.english: I don't feel like the economy has really recovered.

examples.japanese: {海外|かいがい}に{住|す}んで{初|はじ}めて、{日本|にほん}の{便利|べんり}さを{実感|じっかん}した。
examples.english: Only after living overseas did I truly appreciate how convenient Japan is.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもが{成長|せいちょう}するにつれて、{時間|じかん}の{早|はや}さを{実感|じっかん}するようになった。
examples.english: As my children grow, I've come to truly feel how fast time passes.

examples.japanese: {病気|びょうき}をして{初|はじ}めて{健康|けんこう}のありがたさを{実感|じっかん}した。
examples.english: Only after getting sick did I truly realize how precious health is.

notes:
COMMON PATTERNS:
・{実感|じっかん}がある/ない (to feel/not feel like it's real)
・{実感|じっかん}がわく (a sense of reality emerges)
・{実感|じっかん}する (to truly feel/realize)
・〜を{実感|じっかん}する (to feel ~ firsthand)

COMMON EXPRESSION:
・{実感|じっかん}が{湧|わ}かない (can't feel it's real)

SIMILAR WORDS:
・{実際|じっさい} - actually, in reality
・{体験|たいけん} - experience
・{痛感|つうかん} - keenly feeling (often negative)

[Register: Neutral]
